However, accurately quantifying airway dilatation is challenging due to the intricate nature of airway structures and the limitations of conventional imaging techniques.  This study introduces a novel method for airway dilatation quantification, which leverages a deep learning-based approach to segment airway structures from CT images.  Our method employs a 3D U-Net architecture to segment airway structures, followed by the calculation of airway lumen volume and the identification of airway dilatation.  Our method was evaluated on a dataset of 100 CT images from COPD patients, and the results demonstrate its effectiveness in accurately quantifying airway dilatation.  Our method achieved a Dice score of 0.89, a Hausdorff distance of 2.3 mm, and a volumetric error of 15.2%, which are significantly better than conventional methods.  Our method has the potential to improve the diagnosis and treatment of COPD by providing a more accurate and reliable method for airway dilatation quantification.
